title: CRLR/41/2012 of SMT. SUNITA RAWAT Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ANR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.41 of 2012
Smt. Sunita Rawat
ÖÖÖ..Revisionist
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & another
ÖÖÖRespondents
Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, Advocate, for the revisionist
Mrs. Mamta Bisht, AGA for the State/respondent no.1
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate, for respondent no.2
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
The revision challenges the judgment and order dated
17.12.2011 passed by the Sessions Judge, Dehradun in
Criminal Appeal No.75 of 2011, titled as Vinod Rawat Vs. State
of Uttarakhand and another.
Admittedly, revisionist is the wife of respondent no.2 but
she is living in segregation along with her minor daughter.
The Court has been apprised that the divorce proceedings
between the couple are also underway.
Revisionist, while litigating her husband under Section
23(1) inter alia, claiming relief under Sections 12, 18, 19, 20,
21 and 22 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence
Act, 2005 (hereinafter to be referred as the Act) moved
application for interim maintenance, which was granted by
learned Judicial Magistrate First, Dehradun vide order dated
10.8.2011 to the tune of Rs.7,000/- per mensem for the
purpose. This order was challenged by way of filing a criminal
appeal no.75/2011, as indicated above. The Sessions Judge
was of the view that since it was simply an interim
maintenance application and learned Magistrate had yet to
consider other liabilities of respondent no.2, the appellate

court reduced the interim maintenance @Rs.3,500/- per
month.
It has been argued on behalf of revisionist that the
amount is so meager that she cannot survive along with
daughter while living in segregation and at the same time,
fighting litigation against her husband.
This Court also do agree with the arguments put forth by
learned counsel. Learned Sessions Judge has not reasoned
his order for reducing the amount of maintenance nor he took
into consideration the annual income of Rs.3.00 lakhs, as
admitted by respondent no.2 himself. Even if it is accepted
that respondent no.2 resides along with his mother and sister,
then also the amount of Rs.7,000/- per month to be incurred
for maintenance of his wife along with her daughter is not
enough.
Thus, this revision has force and liable to be allowed.
Revision is hereby allowed. Impugned judgment and order
dated 17.12.2011 passed by the Sessions Judge, Dehradun in
criminal appeal no.75/2011 is set aside. At the same time,
the order dated 10.8.2011 passed by the Judicial Magistrate
First, Dehradun in Misc. Case No.60/2011, granting interim
maintenance @Rs.7,000/- per mensem is hereby sustained
from the date of moving of application by the revisionist-wife.
It is hereby made clear that this order, confirming the
interim maintenance, will not come in the way while
adjudicating the amount for final maintenance.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
11.09.2012
Rdang
